newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Norilsk may give up some of unit's shares.
newsitem.headline: Russian Norilsk may give up some of unit's shares.

text.p: Russian metals group Norilsk Nickel will consider transferrring a controlling stake in one of its affiliates to the Krasnoyarsk regional administration, a senior regional official said on Monday.

First Deputy Governor Vladimir Kuzmin told Reuters RAO Norilsky Nikel may transfer a controlling stake in AO Krastsvetmet, a precious metals refiner, to the Krasnoyarsk regional administration for tax arrears.
"Such proposals have been discussed," he said. "We, on our part, have signed the documents. Now the Norilsk Nickel board will consider it."
Norilsk Nickel spokesman Anatoly Komrakov said the company had not yet set the date for the board meeting.

Norilsk Nickel is considering a transfer of the stake to the regional administration for tax arrears in accordance with the government plan of restructuring companies' tax arrears. According to the scheme, Norilsk Nickel will have five years to restructure the debt and 10 years to restructure fines.
If Norilsk Nickel fails to make two consequent current tax payments, Krasnoyarsk regional administration will become an owner of Krastsvetmet shares.
Komrakov said Norilsk Nickel Metallurgical Combine's tax arrears to Krasnoyarsk region amounted to 1.20 billion roubles ($2.07 million) on January 1, 1997.
